1_node_sequence_walk.note: Full 80-node internal walk (each stage's A_Cap/A_to_Y_delay/Y_Ron/Y/next-net hops) confirmed identical structure; compacted here to per-stage model names.

5_b_independence_check_RowClockFanout0_E.array_geometry_coupling: NONE -- SitePitch/array_area/TotalLoadCapPerBit removed entirely by this fix; the new EnBuf chain's own sizing depends only on N (via n_enable_stages) and each stage's own fixed cache lookup, never on B or array area.
5_b_independence_check_RowClockFanout0_E.root_cause_of_residual_spread: A pre-existing, unrelated DFFRAM bug, NOT introduced by this fix and NOT array-geometry: the 'Connect DFF array' loop in constructModel() calls portConnect(dffs[i], "CK", row_ck_sources[i]) once per bit index (number_bits times) on the SAME single dffs[i] instance, and ElectricalModel::portConnect() adds a new addDownstreamNode edge on every call with no de-duplication -- so whatever drives row_ck_sources[i] (INV_CKGate1_i directly, at RowClockFanout=0) sees the DFF's real CK-pin capacitance counted B times in getTotalDownstreamCap(), not once. This is the same class of bug BufferCharacteristics.cc's own comment already documents for the parallel 'D' pin loop. It affects the INV_CKGate1_i -> DFF.CK segment, which is DOWNSTREAM of and untouched by this task's EnableBuf chain -- out of scope to fix here (touches the D-path fanout too, not just clock distribution), flagged rather than silently patched.

6_depth_scaling_B32.note: EnableFanout=2 chosen as the fixed-fanout curve because it is the empirically-best value at every N>=8 (see item 2); N=4's true best is EnableFanout=0 (direct connection, chain overhead not worth it at only 4 gates) -- included in the 'best_per_point' variant instead, not the fixed-EnableFanout=2 curve.

8_note: No stored BroadcastHTree baseline was given for leak_ram or e_write, so only area and e_read have deltas computed; leak_ram/e_write are reported as current absolute values only.

side_finding_not_fixed.description: Discovered while diagnosing item 5's residual B-dependence, NOT part of this task's scope (DFFRAM.cc's 'Connect DFF array' loop, pre-existing before this task): portConnect(dffs[i], "CK", row_ck_sources[i]) and portConnect(dffs[i], "D", "In", n) are both called number_bits times per row on the same single dffs[i] instance (dffs[i] represents ALL B bits via an area/power weight multiplier, addSubInstances(dffs[i], number_bits), not B separate timing-graph instances) -- portConnect adds a fresh addDownstreamNode edge every call with no de-duplication, so the real downstream fanout capacitance seen by whatever drives CK (or D) into a row is counted number_bits times, not once.
side_finding_not_fixed.impact_on_this_fix: None on the EnableBuf chain itself (upstream of this, N-dependent only). Affects the INV_CKGate1_i -> DFF.CK segment (with or without RowBuf), which is why item 5 shows a residual, non-array-geometry B-dependence even with the row-enable path's own contribution isolated.
side_finding_not_fixed.not_fixed_because: Out of this task's file/scope restriction (DFFRAM.cc's row-enable chain only) and touches the D-path fanout too, which is a separate concern from clock/enable distribution -- flagging for a future, separately-scoped task rather than silently patching it here.
